headline.purpose: The page title, one per page.

title.purpose: A display's name on its card, the screen's name in the editor (at 620), an empty state's title.

section-title.purpose: A card's title, the claim panel's and the sign-in form's.

body.purpose: Running text, fact values and table cells; forms at a 44rem measure.

label.purpose: Buttons, field labels and table headings; hints and notes take the size at 400.

caption.purpose: A display's caption and a day strip's names and hours; badges and tags at 560 to 580.

code.purpose: The YAML editor, and anything typed or copied verbatim (0.9em inline, 12px for a source's data).

wordmark.purpose: The lowercase name after its mark.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: The only shadow: what floats over the page (the editor's completion list and hover tooltips).

shadows.name: display-edge
shadows.purpose: The hairline ring around a display's screen; a line, not depth.

shadows.name: cell-focus
shadows.purpose: The halo on the active cell of a claim code.

shadows.name: focus-outline
shadows.purpose: Focus on every control; a field's focus is its ink border inside a 2px outline of the ink at 45%, offset 0.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Background, border and colour changes on hover and press; a disclosure chevron's turn.

motion.name: busy
motion.purpose: A display panel dims to 60% while its image is replaced.

motion.name: state-ended
motion.purpose: A state badge whose state ended fades to 55% and is struck through.

motion.name: afterimage
motion.value: 2000ms cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.55, 1) forwards; opacity 0.4 to 0, filter blur(0) to blur(1.5px), mix-blend-mode multiply
motion.purpose: The image a display showed before lingers over the new one and fades, as e-paper ghosts after a refresh. Display images only.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every transition and the afterimage end at once.

narrative.overview:
The displays are the subject, and the room around them is quiet. Every screen a device shows sits at its true pixels, white as e-paper is, on a cool paper ground; everything else steps back so a display's own black and white stay the loudest thing on the page. All neutrals share the ink's hue (218) at a whisper of chroma, so the room is one temperature, and the only colour that speaks is a single teal-blue ink that marks what a hand can act on. Amber appears only where a state wants attention; red only where something is removed or has gone wrong.

The density is that of a calm working tool. A sunken rail holds the wordmark, three places and the account; the content column holds white cards on hairlines, one card per concern, and text ranks by weight and colour before size. Light and dark are one system: each colour is a single `light-dark()` pair in `web/src/app/global.css`, the page follows the system scheme, and Settings can pin either theme.

The world refuses the category's dashboard of status tiles and pills. A device's facts are a quiet two-column list, its day is a grey strip with a line at now, and a badge appears only for a state that needs the person. There are no mascots, illustrations or playful flourishes. The ornament the system allows is its name made visible: the mark is a square and the fainter square it leaves behind, and when a display's image changes, the one before lingers under it and fades, as e-paper ghosts after a refresh.
keyCharacteristics: Displays at 1:1 (up to 800 pixels wide) on white, edged by a hairline, with palette, size and scale beneath.
One teal-blue ink at hue 218 for links, the current place, focus, the primary action and what a hand has set.
Cool paper neutrals at the ink's hue; white cards on 1px hairlines with 12px corners.
Schibsted Grotesk for everything; JetBrains Mono only for what is typed or copied verbatim.
Flat at rest; the one shadow belongs to what floats.
Light and dark from one `light-dark()` pair per colour.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: The ink marks what a hand can act on or has set, and nothing else. If a surface needs ink to look finished, it is decorating.

rules.name: The One Temperature Rule
rules.body: Every neutral is hue 218 at chroma 0.02 or less. A new neutral takes the same hue; pure greys and warm greys do not belong in the room.

rules.name: The Held Reserve Rule
rules.body: Amber appears only where a state wants attention; red only for removal and errors. Neither colours a heading, an icon, a chart or a decoration.

rules.name: The Weight Before Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from weight and colour before size. The scale tops out at 26px, and a step down in importance is a step from Deep Slate to Slate to Muted Slate before it is a smaller size.

rules.name: The Verbatim Mono Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono sets only what is typed or copied exactly: YAML, addresses, commands, secret and source names, a source's data, a problem's location. Prose, labels and headings never take it.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Everything is in sentence case. Letter-spacing only tightens headings and the wordmark; nothing is uppercased or tracked out.

rules.name: The Only What Floats Rule
rules.body: Nothing at rest casts a shadow. The overlay shadow is for what floats over the page and for nothing else.

dos: Do show every display image at its true pixels where the column allows (1:1 up to 800px), on Display White with the display-edge ring, with palette, size and scale beneath it.
Do keep the ink (oklch(48% 0.1 218) light, oklch(78% 0.085 218) dark) for links, the current place, focus, the primary action and what a hand has set.
Do declare every colour as one `light-dark()` pair at hue 218 and check both themes.
Do put each concern on its own white card: 12px corners, a 1px hairline, a 16px gutter that widens to 24px from 48rem.
Do rank text by weight and by Deep Slate, Slate and Muted Slate before size; keep body text at 14px on 1.55 and forms at a 44rem measure.
Do show a device state that wants attention as an amber badge beside its name, and keep a state that ends while the page is open, struck through at 55% opacity.
Do open a destructive action with an outlined danger button, say in the confirmation what it does to the device, and finish it with a solid danger button beside a quiet Cancel.
Do reserve the afterimage for display images: the image before, multiplied over the new one, fading from 40% to none and blurring to 1.5px over 2000ms, and 1ms under reduced motion.
donts: Don't build dashboards of status tiles, stat cards or rows of status pills; a device's facts are a two-column list of Muted Slate labels and plain values.
Don't use the ink as decoration: no ink headings, bands, gradients or tinted icons; an icon takes the colour of its text.
Don't introduce pure or warm greys; every neutral is hue 218 at chroma 0.02 or less.
Don't give anything at rest a shadow for depth; the overlay shadow is only for what floats.
Don't use amber or red for anything but a state that wants attention, removal and errors.
Don't set prose, labels or headings in JetBrains Mono, and don't uppercase or track out a label.
Don't draw on, tint or crop a display's image, or scale it above its true pixels; the editor's optional guides are the only marks laid over it.
Don't add mascots, cute illustration or playful copy; Afterimage is a calm tool.
